entry: American actress and director. Bates won the Academy Award for Best Actress for playing Annie Wilkes in the psychological thriller *Misery* (1990). She was further nominated for Oscars for *Primary Colors* (1998), *About Schmidt* (2002) and *Richard Jewell* (2019). Bates won Primetime Emmy Awards for *Two and a Half Men* (2012) and *American Horror Story: Coven* (2013). Since 2024 she has starred as the title character in the [[CBS]] series *Matlock*. After developing lymphedema following a double mastectomy, she became a spokesperson for the Lymphatic Education & Research Network.

Endorheic lake in the Far North region of [[South Australia]]. The lake lies some 700 km (430 mi) north of [[Adelaide]] and is the largest ephemeral endorheic lake on the Australian continent, covering over 9,000 sq km (3,500 sq mi). It contains the lowest natural point in Australia, at approximately 15 m (49 ft) below sea level. The lake is most often empty and fills mostly when flooding occurs upstream in the Channel Country. It has filled completely only three times between 1860 and 2025. Named after Edward John Eyre, the first European to see it in 1840, it was renamed in December 2012 to include its Aboriginal name, Kati Thanda. Native title is held mainly by the Arabana people. Donald Campbell set a land speed record of 403.10 mph (648.73 km/h) for a four-wheeled vehicle on the salt flats in 1964.

British actress and businesswoman in Hindi-language films. Born in [[British Hong Kong]], Kaif began modeling as a teenager. She made her acting debut in *Boom* (2003), a critical and commercial failure, and found commercial success in Bollywood with *Maine Pyaar Kyun Kiya?* (2005) and *Namastey London* (2007). She is noted for action films and dancing, and her hits include *Ek Tha Tiger* (2012), *Dhoom 3* (2013) and *Bang Bang!* (2014). One of India's highest-paid actresses, she launched the cosmetics line Kay Beauty in 2019.

Sea between [[Denmark]] and [[Sweden]], bounded by the [[Skagerrak]] to the north and by [[Zealand]] and the Danish Straits to the south. Jutland lies to the west, and the Swedish provinces of Bohuslän, Västergötland, Halland and Scania to the east. The [[Baltic Sea]] drains into the Kattegat through the Danish Straits. Its name derives from Dutch *katte* ('cat's') and *gat* ('gate, passage'), referring to a passage so tight that a cat would have difficulty squeezing through. The sea is shallow and hazardous to navigate, with many sandy and stony reefs and shifting currents. Artificial channels and dredging have eased navigation, and a light signaling network protects heavy international traffic. Major ports include [[Gothenburg]] and Aarhus.

American singer, songwriter and television personality. Her breakthrough album, *One of the Boys* (2008), produced the U.S. number-one single "I Kissed a Girl." *Teenage Dream* (2010) became the only album by a woman to produce five U.S. number-one singles. Perry is one of the best-selling music artists of all time, with estimated sales of over 151 million records worldwide. She served as a judge on [[American Idol]] from 2018 to 2024 and was named a [[UNICEF]] Goodwill Ambassador in 2013. She is an advocate for LGBT rights and women's rights.

Soviet massacre of Polish military officers and intelligentsia in 1940. Between April and May 1940, the NKVD secret police executed nearly 22,000 Polish officers, police, border guards and intelligentsia on the orders of [[Joseph Stalin|Stalin]]. Some of the mass graves, in the Katyn forest, were first discovered by Nazi German forces in 1943, and the Soviet Union blamed Nazi Germany for the killings. It acknowledged and condemned the NKVD killings in December 1989. A 2009 resolution of the Polish parliament's Sejm stated that the massacre bore the hallmarks of genocide. In 2010 the Russian State Duma condemned Stalin and other Soviet officials for ordering it.

Pepper-family plant (*Piper methysticum*) native to the Pacific Islands, and the drink made from its root. Kava is a traditional ceremonial and social beverage in [[Polynesia]], [[Micronesia]] and [[Melanesia]]. Its psychoactive effects are comparable to alcohol's but involve no significant cognitive impairment or addiction risk. The plant was domesticated in northern [[Vanuatu]] around 3,000 years ago. Many countries banned or restricted kava in 2002 over safety concerns. The [[World Health Organization]] concluded that moderate consumption of traditional water-based kava presents an "acceptably low level of health risk," but that extracts made with organic solvents may be linked to liver injury.

Transfrontier conservation area in [[Southern Africa]]. It spans the borders of [[Angola]], [[Botswana]], [[Namibia]], [[Zambia]] and [[Zimbabwe]] and is the second-largest nature and landscape conservation area in the world. It includes a major part of the upper Zambezi River and Okavango basins and Delta, and its center is at the confluence of the Zambezi and Chobe rivers. The area covers 520,000 sq km (200,000 sq mi) and incorporates parks including Chobe, Hwange and Mana Pools. It is home to approximately 250,000 African elephants, the largest population in the world. A treaty among the five governments was signed on August 18, 2011, and the area officially opened on March 15, 2012.

Nomadic Turkic state in [[Central Asia]], c. 1465 to the early 19th century. It emerged after the fragmentation of the [[Golden Horde]]. By the end of the 15th century the Kazakhs controlled the steppe east of the [[Caspian Sea]] and north of the [[Aral Sea]], and under Kasym Khan their authority reached the [[Ural Mountains]]. The khanate declined in the 17th and 18th centuries and, after the death of Tauke Khan, split into three independent khanates known as zhuzes. Ablai Khan reunited the Kazakhs, but after his death in 1781 the zhuzes fractured again, and their khans were appointed by the Russian government. The institution of the khanate was abolished in the [[Russian Empire]] in 1822–1824. It was the first nation-state in Central Asia created by the modern Kazakh ethnic group itself.

Kipchak branch [[Turkic languages|Turkic]] language and the official language of [[Kazakhstan]]. It is closely related to Nogai, Kyrgyz and Karakalpak, and is agglutinative, with vowel harmony. Ethnologue recognizes three mutually intelligible dialect groups: North-Eastern Kazakh, the most widely spoken and the basis of the official language; Southern Kazakh; and Western Kazakh. Kazakh has official status in the Altai Republic of Russia, and over one million speakers in Xinjiang, China, use a modified Perso-Arabic script. Kazakhs wrote in the [[Arabic script]] until about 1929, and the Soviet regime later imposed Latin and then [[Cyrillic script|Cyrillic]] scripts. A 2017 decree ordered a change to Latin script, scheduled to be phased in from 2023 to 2031.

Landlocked country in [[Central Asia]] with a portion extending into [[Eastern Europe]]. Its capital is [[Astana]]; the largest city, Almaty, was the capital until 1997. Kazakhstan is the ninth-largest country by land area and the largest landlocked country. Ethnic Kazakhs form a majority, and the country is officially secular with a Muslim majority. The area has been inhabited since the Paleolithic era, and it was subjugated by the [[Mongol Empire]] in the 13th century. After the [[Kazakh Khanate]] fragmented, the territory was absorbed by the [[Russian Empire]]. It became a Soviet republic and was the last Soviet republic to declare independence, in 1991. Nursultan Nazarbayev led the country from independence until his resignation in 2019. Kazakhstan accounts for 60% of Central Asia's GDP, mainly through oil and gas. Critics describe its government as authoritarian.

Capital and largest city of [[Tatarstan]], Russia. Kazan lies at the confluence of the [[Volga]] and Kazanka rivers and has a population of over 1.3 million. It was the capital of the [[Khanate of Kazan]], which [[Ivan the Terrible]] conquered in the 16th century, after which the city became part of the [[Tsardom of Russia]]. Pugachev's Rebellion (1773–75) seized and largely destroyed the city, which was rebuilt under [[Catherine the Great]]. In 1920 Kazan became capital of the Tatar Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic, and after the Soviet Union dissolved it remained capital of Tatarstan. The Kazan Kremlin is a [[UNESCO]] World Heritage Site, and the city hosted the 2013 Summer Universiade and the BRICS Games in 2024.

Russian avant-garde painter and art theorist, founder of Suprematism. Born in Kiev, in present-day Ukraine, to an ethnic Polish family, he worked mainly in Russia. In 1915 he developed Suprematism, a system of pure geometric abstraction on monochromatic grounds. His *Black Square* (1915), first shown at the Last Futurist Exhibition 0,10 in Petrograd, marked a decisive break with representational painting. In 1918 he taught in Vitebsk alongside [[Marc Chagall]], and in 1919 he founded the UNOVIS artists collective. He was briefly arrested by the OGPU in 1930. By the early 1930s Stalin's cultural policy and the imposition of Socialist Realism had pushed him back to figurative painting. His work influenced later abstract artists, including Ad Reinhardt and the Minimalists. The [[Museum of Modern Art]] staged a major exhibition of his work in 1936.

National park and World Heritage Site in the Indian state of [[Assam]]. It lies on the edge of the [[Brahmaputra River]] and encompasses tropical moist broadleaf forests, tall elephant grass and marshland dotted with lakes, or beels. The park hosts populations of the Indian rhinoceros, [[Asian elephant]], wild water buffalo, swamp deer, [[Tiger|tigers]] and fishing cat, and it is an Important Bird Area. After Mary Curzon failed to see an Indian rhinoceros on a visit in 1904, measures were taken to protect the species, and the Kaziranga Proposed Reserve Forest was created on June 1, 1905. It was renamed the Kaziranga Wildlife Sanctuary in 1950. Floods on the Brahmaputra have caused losses of wildlife, and in 2024 six dead rhinos and hundreds of deer were counted as drowned.

Japanese-born British novelist, screenwriter and short-story writer. Born in [[Nagasaki]], Japan, he moved to Britain in 1960 at age five. His first novels, *A Pale View of Hills* and *An Artist of the Floating World*, explored Japanese identity in a mournful tone. Later works drew on science fiction and historical fiction while keeping a focus on the outsider's perspective and the search for an unattainable truth. He won the [[Booker Prize]] in 1989 for *The Remains of the Day*, which was adapted into a film in 1993. *Time* named *Never Let Me Go* the best novel of 2005. He was awarded the 2017 Nobel Prize in Literature.

Canadian actor and musician. Born in [[Beirut]] and raised in [[Toronto]], Reeves rose to fame with the science-fiction comedy *Bill & Ted's Excellent Adventure* (1989) and became an action star in *Point Break* (1991) and *Speed* (1994). He played Neo in *The Matrix* (1999) and its sequels, and the title assassin in the *John Wick* series, which began in 2014. He made his feature directorial debut with *Man of Tai Chi* (2013). Reeves is a member of the band Dogstar and co-founded the motorcycle manufacturer ARCH Motorcycle.

Fermented milk drink similar to a thin [[Yogurt|yogurt]]. It is made by inoculating the milk of cows, goats or sheep with kefir grains, a symbiotic culture of bacteria and yeasts. Traditional kefir is fermented at ambient temperature, generally overnight, producing a sour, slightly carbonated and slightly alcoholic beverage. The word is of North Caucasian origin and It is attested in Russian from the 1870s. Kefir is a common drink in [[West Asia]] and Central and Eastern Europe. It spread from the former Soviet Union to the rest of Europe, Canada, Japan and the United States by the early 21st century.

British actress known for independent films and period dramas. Knightley played Elizabeth Swann in the *Pirates of the Caribbean* films (2003–2007, 2017) and gained recognition in *Bend It Like Beckham* (2002) and *Love Actually* (2003). She received Academy Award nominations for Best Actress for *Pride & Prejudice* (2005) and Best Supporting Actress for *The Imitation Game* (2014). She has appeared in two West End productions and starred on Broadway in *Thérèse Raquin* (2015). She is outspoken on social issues and has worked extensively with Amnesty International, Oxfam and Comic Relief.

American artist and social activist. Emerging from the downtown art and graffiti scenes of [[New York City]] in the early 1980s, Haring drew animated chalk figures on unused subway advertising panels, bridging street art and [[Pop art]]. He created more than 50 public murals between 1982 and 1989, many for hospitals, schools and community spaces. His work addressed anti-apartheid activism, the crack epidemic, homosexuality, safe sex and AIDS awareness. He opened the Pop Shop in 1986 to sell affordable merchandise. After his death from AIDS-related complications, the Whitney Museum of American Art organized a retrospective of his work in 1997.

English guitarist, singer and songwriter. He is an original member of [[The Rolling Stones]], and his songwriting partnership with [[Mick Jagger]] is one of the most successful in history. Richards's guitar style has been a trademark of the band, and his drug use and romantic involvements brought him press notoriety. He was inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in 1989. *Rolling Stone* ranked him fourth among the 100 best guitarists in 2011. He also played Captain Teague, father of Jack Sparrow, in two *Pirates of the Caribbean* films.

American singer-songwriter and television personality. Clarkson rose to fame after winning the first season of [[American Idol]]. Her debut single, "A Moment Like This," was the best-selling single of the year in the United States. Her album *Breakaway* (2004) is one of the best-selling albums of the 21st century. With over 82 million records sold worldwide, she has won three [[Grammy Awards]]. She coached on *The Voice* for ten seasons (2018–2026) and hosted *The Kelly Clarkson Show* from 2019 to 2026.

American actress and talk show host. Since 2001 she has co-hosted the syndicated morning talk show *Live! with Kelly and Mark*, alongside co-hosts including Regis Philbin, Michael Strahan and Ryan Seacrest. Her best-known acting roles were Hayley Vaughan on the ABC soap opera *All My Children* and Faith Fairfield on the ABC sitcom *Hope & Faith*. With her husband, actor Mark Consuelos, she owns the [[New York City]]-based production company Milojo. In 2014 *The Hollywood Reporter* named her one of the Most Powerful People in Media.

Large brown seaweeds in the order Laminariales. Kelp comprises about 30 genera and, despite using photosynthesis in chloroplasts, is not a plant but a stramenopile. It grows in dense, forest-like stands in shallow temperate and Arctic oceans, where the water is nutrient-rich and between 6 and 14 °C (43 and 57 °F). Macrocystis and Nereocystis can grow as fast as half a meter a day, reaching 30 to 80 meters. Kelp blades are held up by gas-filled bladders in some species, and the stipes are anchored to the seabed by a holdfast. Sea urchins can reduce kelp beds to barrens. Through the 19th century the word kelp referred to seaweeds burned to obtain soda ash, primarily [[Sodium carbonate]].

American actor and comedian. Grammer is known for playing psychiatrist Dr. Frasier Crane on the [[NBC]] sitcoms [[Cheers]] (1984–1993) and [[Frasier]] (1993–2004), one of the longest-running roles played by a single live-action actor in primetime television history. He has received six Emmy Awards, three Golden Globe Awards and a Tony Award. In film he played Dr. Hank McCoy, known as Beast, in the *X-Men* films beginning with *X-Men: The Last Stand* (2006). He voices Sideshow Bob on [[The Simpsons]]. In 2016 he won a Tony Award for Best Musical as a producer of *The Color Purple*.

Base unit of temperature in the [[International System of Units]] (SI), symbol K. The kelvin scale is an absolute temperature scale that starts at [[Absolute zero]], taken to be 0 K. A rise of one kelvin equals a rise of one degree [[Celsius]], and a Celsius temperature is converted to kelvins by adding 273.15. The scale was first proposed in 1848 by William Thomson, later [[Lord Kelvin]], whose paper gave a value of −273 °C for absolute zero. The kelvin was formally added to the SI in 1954, when 273.16 K was defined as the triple point of water. The 2019 revision of the SI instead fixes the Boltzmann constant at exactly 1.380649×10⁻²³ joules per kelvin.
